correctness.rationale: The proof establishes for every integer r the biconditional that K is \(r\)-conic exactly when its simplicial total-domination number exceeds r. Both directions explicitly construct the corresponding witness. The infinite case is handled by proving that absence of any total-dominating set is equivalent to K being a cone. Join additivity follows from an exact factorwise characterization of total-dominating sets in a join. A separate exhaustive implementation checks all labeled complexes on at most four vertices and 144 small join pairs.

originality.rationale: The checked conicity literature and the checked total-domination literature develop the two definitions separately. Barmak proves a one-sided join conicity bound, whereas the present identity yields equality for maximal conicity. No inspected source states the parameter identity or the exact join equality.
residual_risks: The 2006 Aharoni--Berger full text was inaccessible through the attempted lawful routes, so its exact wording was checked through a later thesis rather than the original article.
An obscure or unindexed post-2021 source could have noticed the same equivalence or exact join equality under different terminology.
The theorem is elementary once the two definitions are juxtaposed; originality is therefore especially sensitive to unindexed observations.

value.rationale: The finding is a general structural lemma rather than a parameter increment or finite recomputation. It identifies maximal conicity exactly with an established domination invariant and converts the published join lower bound into equality. This creates a direct transfer principle between domination calculations and conicity-based homotopy-connectivity arguments. Its value does not depend on claiming novel connectivity bounds obtained by substitution.
